name: Lakeshore Tourism · Project Management Demo
tagline: PMT Console · Cal Rogers' Tuesday morning
builder: the demo builder (Mesh, Claude Code, or a teammate)

extra_notes.title: This is the bundled sample.
extra_notes.html: Copy examples/lakeshore-pm/demo.json, swap in your own steps, then run python3 scripts/build.py your-demo.json.

reset: Shoot Lakeshore Trail landmarks: End Date back to 9/28
Shoot state park lodge interiors: Assigned To back to Vanessa Central
Draft: North Shore feature: Sign-off back to Submitted
agent_rules: PMT is a managed package (Salesforce Labs). Configure around it; don't edit its metadata.

steps.t: Sign in and open the PMT Console
c: Sign in to the VisitLakeshore demo org
App Launcher → PMT Console (not standard PMT)
e: Console app opens with workspace tabs
You're logged in as the user whose name should show as Cal Rogers on the dashboard
steps.f: If only standard PMT shows, the console app isn't assigned to your profile. Assign the app, or use standard PMT and expect clunkier tab navigation.

steps.t: Deck check: title date + slide order
c: Open the Travel Lakeshore – Project Management deck (the 9-slide version)
Check the title slide, then flip through to 'From Challenge to Solved'
e: The title slide date reads October 9, 2026. It currently says September 25.

Order: Who is Salesforce → Public Sector → Current Challenges → Meet Cal Rogers → What Cal Is Up Against (Oct 2 press date) → Cal's Journey (5 steps), where the live demo starts → From Challenge to Solved → Thank you
steps.f: The script's slide numbers (5–10) are off by one compared with this 9-slide deck. Go by slide titles, not numbers.

c: Dashboards → Project Portfolio → Refresh
e: The As of timestamp shows today
The running user shows Cal Rogers
steps.f: If it shows a different user, change the dashboard's running user, or say it's Cal's view and move on.

steps.t: Write down the golden-record baseline (for the reset)
c: Travel Guide → Tasks → use the row-action ▼ → View on each task below
e: Shoot Lakeshore Trail landmarks: End Date = Sep 28
Shoot state park lodge interiors: Assigned To = Vanessa Central
Draft: North Shore feature: Sign-off = Submitted
Resources: write down the current allocations, or take a screenshot of them
steps.f: If any value already differs, a previous run wasn't reset. Fix it now using the Data Reset list (step 4.1).

c: Choose a spare PMT project with tasks you can change. Clone the Travel Guide from its template if you can.
Type its name in the sidebar box
e: The test project has: an assigned task you can reassign, a task with an End Date, a task with Sign-off = Submitted routed to you, and 2+ tasks for the mass status change
Its Chatter tab has at least one existing thread
steps.f: If there's no spare project and no time to clone one, run Phase 2 on the Travel Guide and do the full Data Reset (4.1) right afterward. Confirm with the builder: is there a test project?

steps.t: Opportunity: Harbor City Tourism – Lakeshore Trail Content Series
c: Opportunities → Harbor City Tourism - Lakeshore Trail Content Series
e: Amount $65,000
Linked project shows Lakeshore Trail Guide
steps.f: If there's no project link, the lookup or related list is missing from the layout. Tell the builder.

c: Stay on the opportunity and wait about 10 seconds
e: The Murray (Agentforce) summary panel renders with deal history and next actions
Nothing in it is inaccurate or embarrassing
steps.f: If it doesn't render within about 10 seconds, plan to skip it live, as the script says. Note how long it took.

c: PMT Console → 2026 Annual Travel Guide → Revenue tab
e: Budget Goal $150,000
$115,000 closed-won, 77% of goal
$8,500 in pipeline
The list shows the opportunities that fund this project
steps.f: If the numbers are off, an opportunity's stage or project link changed. Check the per-project funding table in the script.

steps.t: Summary tab: health, phases, period toggle
c: Click the Summary tab
Toggle Weekly → Monthly → Quarterly (top right)
e: Health is green / On Track
6 phases: Content Planning done, Photography wrapping up, Editorial Writing underway
The toggle changes the view each time
steps.f: If the phase statuses look stale, roll-ups may not have recalculated. Tell the builder.

c: Summary → Milestone List button → read it → close the modal
e: Editorial freeze Sep 15
Press-ready files Oct 2
Warehouse delivery Dec 30
steps.f: Note: on Oct 9, the editorial freeze and press dates are already past. Decide how to phrase it (see the note at the top).

c: Find where the project shows it came from a template (field, related record or template object)
e: Something on screen you can point to when you say this project was created from a template
steps.f: Confirm with the builder: expected ___. If nothing is visible, narrate it without pointing.

c: Click the Timeline tab. Don't drag anything.
e: Bars are grouped by phase. Green = completed, blue = in progress (Lakeshore Trail photo shoot 75%, North Shore feature), gray = upcoming
A red Today line
The October crunch is visible (Editorial, Design & Layout, Review all overlap)
steps.f: If the Today line sits after the in-progress bars, the story looks late. Consider shifting the demo dates (see the note at the top).

c: Click the Resources tab
Click Edit Allocations, look at the grid, then click Cancel
e: Cal at 30% as Project Manager
Vanessa at 40% in Sep–Oct
Vince picks up during the editorial crunch
The grid is editable, and Cancel leaves everything unchanged
steps.f: If the grid doesn't open, check component permissions. Tell the builder.

steps.t: Tasks tab: In Progress filter + row action
c: Click the Tasks tab → filter to In Progress
On one row, click ▼ → View. Don't click the cell value.
e: 3 tasks: Vince on the North Shore feature (~halfway), Vanessa on the Lakeshore Trail photo shoot (75%), Valerie on the Lakeshore Trail road trip itinerary
▼ → View opens the record without starting an inline edit
steps.f: If the count isn't 3, a task's status changed since the build. Reset it, or adjust your talk track.

steps.t: Approval setup on North Shore draft (look only)
c: Open Draft: North Shore feature (▼ → View)
Find the Approval History component
e: Sign-off = Submitted
Approval History shows it submitted by Vince and pending with Cal (you)
An Approve action is available to you
steps.f: If Approve isn't offered, the running user isn't the approver. The fallback is flipping the picklist.

c: Project → Chatter & Activity tab
Then the Files tab
e: At least one existing thread with a Reply option (the compose box doesn't render on managed objects, which is expected)
The Files tab shows project files (brand assets, drafts)
steps.f: If there's no thread to reply to, the builder needs to seed one. If Files is empty, confirm with the builder: expected ___.

c: Dashboards → Project Portfolio
e: Health donut shows 6 projects, all on track
Project Detail, Portfolio Ownership and Resource Assignments components all render
The completion gauge shows 226% (a known quirk, so don't dwell on it)
steps.f: If a component errors, refresh. If it still errors, tell the builder which component.

c: Open the Command Center tab
Spot-check 2 projects' Revenue tabs (e.g. Lakeshore Trail Guide, May Conference)
e: KPI cards, team workload and project pipeline all render
Pipeline shows $10.7M, which is all org opportunities (255). The Lakeshore Tourism figure to quote is $635K across 16 opps.
Lakeshore Trail Guide $127,000 of $175K · May Conference $90,000 of $95K
steps.f: If Command Center doesn't load, skip it live. It's the custom LWC example.

phases.name: Phase 2 · Action tests on the test record (demo order)

c: Test project → Resources → Edit Allocations
Change one October value → Save
e: Saves without an error
The allocation table and totals update
steps.f: If you get a save error, check field-level security on the allocation object. Tell the builder the exact error text.

c: Tasks → open the shoot task (▼ → View) → change Assigned To from Vanessa to Vince West → Save
e: Saves, and the task list shows Vince
The Resources and Assignments views reflect the change (if they're designed to)
steps.f: If the user lookup can't find Vince, the persona user or contact is missing or inactive.

c: Open the landmarks shoot task → change End Date Sep 28 → Oct 3 → Save
Go back to the Summary tab
e: Saves
The phase table on Summary updates on its own, as the talk track says
steps.f: If Summary doesn't update, a roll-up flow isn't firing. Either drop the line 'updates automatically' or get it fixed.

c: Open the draft task with Sign-off = Submitted → Approval History → Approve
e: Status changes to Approved
Approval History shows your approval with a timestamp
No error. Any email alert goes only to your own test address
steps.f: If approval fails, use the fallback of flipping the Sign-off picklist, and tell the builder. If an email alert fires, check who received it.

c: Tasks list → check two rows → Change Status → pick a status → Save
e: Both tasks update in one action
steps.f: If the button is missing, the list view or managed-package action isn't available to you.

c: Chatter & Activity → Reply on an existing thread with a test message
e: The reply posts and appears in the thread
steps.f: If the reply box is missing too, the live fallback is to narrate it and show the existing thread. Tell the builder.

c: Timeline → drag one bar a few days → reopen the task
e: The task's dates changed to match the drag
steps.f: If dates don't save, drop the line 'those changes save automatically' from the talk track.

c: Refresh the test project's Summary, then the Project Portfolio dashboard
e: Phase % and health reflect the test changes
The dashboard refreshes without errors
steps.f: Confirm with the builder: expected roll-up behavior is ___.

c: Reload the Harbor City Tourism opportunity and time how long until Murray renders
e: It renders consistently, and the content matches the deal
steps.f: If it's slow or inconsistent, plan to skip it in the opening and mention it at the close instead.

c: On the test project, and on the Travel Guide if you used it:
Shoot Lakeshore Trail landmarks: End Date back to Sep 28
Shoot state park lodge interiors: Assigned To back to Vanessa Central
Draft: North Shore feature: Sign-off back to Submitted
Revert any allocation, status or timeline changes
e: Every value matches your baseline from step 0.4
steps.f: If the approval can't be reset to Submitted, recall or resubmit it, or ask the builder for a reset script.

c: Travel Guide → Tasks, Approval History, Resources, Revenue
e: Every value matches step 0.4
Revenue still shows $115K / 77% / $8.5K
In Progress filter still shows 3 tasks
steps.f: If anything drifted, fix it now, not tomorrow morning.

c: Refresh the Project Portfolio dashboard on the morning of the demo
Open tabs in demo order: Deck → Opportunity → Travel Guide → Dashboard → Command Center
Close everything else
e: Tabs are in click-path order, and the dashboard timestamp shows today

steps.t: Script fixes confirmed with the AE
c: Check the items in the note at the top of this page
e: Date, customer name, SE name and the pricing line are all settled

title_slide.title: Cal Rogers' Tuesday Morning on Salesforce
title_slide.say: Meet Cal Rogers. He runs content operations for Lakeshore Tourism, and here's how his morning goes on Salesforce.
title_slide.subtitle: Lakeshore Tourism · Project management and sponsorship revenue in the PMT Console

scenes.title: the CMO's four criteria
scenes.card: Useful · Easy to operate · Easy to integrate · Easy to adopt
scenes.say: You told us what matters to your team. Useful, easy to operate, easy to integrate, easy to adopt. We built this around those four things. Let me show you what Cal Rogers' Tuesday morning looks like.

scenes.title: A sponsor signs on
scenes.shot: Harbor City Tourism opp header + PMT Project link
scenes.say: Cal's day starts with good news. Harbor City Tourism just committed to a sixty-five thousand dollar Lakeshore Trail content series. And it's linked directly to the project it funds.

scenes.title: Agentforce on the deal
scenes.shot: Opp with the Agentforce summary panel rendered
scenes.say: On the side, Agentforce is reading the deal history and flagging what needs attention. No digging required.

scenes.title: Revenue tied to the work
scenes.shot: Project Revenue tab: tracker + funding opps
scenes.say: Here's the revenue tab. A budget tracker, closed won against goal, and every opportunity that funds this project. Cal doesn't have to call the sales team. He just looks.

scenes.title: The project at a glance
scenes.shot: Summary tab: health, phases, period toggle
scenes.say: This is what Cal sees every morning. Project health, where each phase stands, all scheduled back from the press date. Weekly for stand-ups, quarterly for leadership.

scenes.title: Milestones
scenes.say: These are the non-negotiable dates. They came from the project template, so Cal never types them twice.

scenes.title: The timeline
scenes.shot: Timeline (Gantt) tab with the Today line
scenes.say: And the view project managers love. Every task across the year, color coded, with a red line for today. You can see exactly where October gets crowded.

scenes.title: Team capacity
scenes.say: Before Cal hands out more work, he checks who actually has room. Every person, every month, one grid.

scenes.title: Work in flight
scenes.shot: Tasks tab filtered to In Progress
scenes.say: Three things in flight. No status update emails. He opens the console and sees it.

scenes.title: Reassign in one click
scenes.shot: Task with Assigned To changed + saved
scenes.say: Vanessa's Lakeshore Trail shoot ran long. One change, and Vince has the lodge shoot.

scenes.title: Adjust the schedule
scenes.shot: Task end date moved + Summary updated
scenes.say: The shoot needs a few more days. Cal moves the date, and the phase table updates on its own.

scenes.title: Approve for print
scenes.say: Vince submitted his feature for review. This is a real approval workflow, with a history of who did what and when. And you could add a second step for the CCMO before anything goes to print.

scenes.title: Bulk updates
scenes.say: Two tasks updated in five seconds.

scenes.title: Talk where the work lives
scenes.say: And the conversation lives on the project. Not in an email thread new people can't find.

scenes.title: the CMO's view
scenes.say: Now zoom out to the CMO's view. Every project, its health, who's carrying the load, all rolled up in one place.

scenes.title: What's possible
scenes.say: And this is what's possible beyond the free app. A custom command center, built on the same platform and the same data.

scenes.title: Crawl, walk, run
scenes.card: Start with three sales seats · PMT is free · grow on one platform
scenes.say: So, useful, easy to operate, easy to integrate, easy to adopt. Start with three sales seats, add project management when you're ready. Crawl, walk, run.
